title: Access Playbook Wizard — compact admin flow for cross-org approvals and cost-sensitive rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, step-by-step "playbook" wizard inside Redwood Console that lets workspace and org admins author cross-workspace approval policies, run a simulated approval scenario, preview the resulting audit-log entries, and surface estimated cost impact for rollout options. The aim is to reduce time-to-configure for security teams, lower misconfiguration risk, and help product teams choose rollout strategies with explicit cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard UI is accessible from Workspace Settings > Access > Create Playbook and as a compact side-panel in the Rollouts view.
Admins can define a policy with: role templates, conditional constraints (time-bound, IP, service principals), and approver chains (single or multi-level).
Simulator runs a synthetic 'request' and shows: approval path, modified permissions, and three previewed audit log rows (create, grant, notify) with timestamps and principal identifiers.
Cost estimator shows incremental token/cold-start cost and projected monthly run-rate for the playbook when applied to N workspaces (configurable).
Prototype includes a compact mobile-friendly layout and a desktop side-panel variant used during on-call and incident workflows.
Design review feedback from Security and Eng resolved (see comments), and a high-fidelity Figma file with annotated interactions is linked.
Accessibility: ARIA labels for wizard steps, keyboard nav, color contrast meets WCAG AA.
related_tasks: PM-4021 (align rollout gating with console feature flags)
ENG-9923 (backend: simulate-approval endpoint + audit-log preview API)
decisions: Keep playbook creation at workspace scope by default; allow elevated org-scope templates for approved org admins.
Simulator will not execute real grants; it will produce a deterministic preview using the same authorization engine but with a dry-run flag.
Cost estimator shows conservative median estimates and links to the Optimize page for detailed tuning recommendations.
tradeoffs: Preview fidelity vs safety: chose dry-run previews to avoid accidental grants but requires close parity with runtime behavior (extra engineering validation).
Compact UI reduces visible detail per step which risks missing edge constraints; tradeoff mitigated by a one-click 'expand step' affordance.
Estimating cost at policy-definition time gives quick signals but may be noisy for heterogeneous workloads—explicit link to historical telemetry is required.
